title: Audit logs & admin activity review - Cascade Bank
summary: Redwood walked Cascade Bank through their audit logging capabilities: what events are captured, available export channels (S3, syslog/SIEM, webhooks), retention defaults and enterprise options, and KMS/customer-managed keys for encryption. Customer requested sample schema, SOC2 report, and a short pilot to stream logs to their S3 for verification.
topics: RBAC/SSO and who triggers admin events
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-20
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Sofia Lin (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Cascade Eng Manager), Rashmi Patel (Cascade Security Lead), Oliver Chen (Cascade IT Ops)

Summary: quick security review focused on audit logs and admin activity, export options, retention, and encryption/KMS.

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ethan from redwood, with sofia our solutions engineer. we're here to run through audit logs and admin activity, make sure it maps to cascade's compliance needs.

[00:18] Liam: hey thanks, short intro from us — rashmi is our security lead, oliver handles infra, i'm product/eng. main goals today: confirm what you capture, how to get it out to our splunk/s3, and retention controls.

[00:35] Sofia: great, i'll start high level then drill into examples. audit logs capture admin actions and system events. admin includes: user creation/deletion, role changes, SSO/SAML config, API key creation/rotation/revocation, model rollouts/rollbacks, dedicated node changes, billing and subscription events, and manual data exports. we also log data plane events at a higher level (e.g., model invocation metadata) but not full user prompt content unless customer enables specific retention.

[01:10] Rashmi: quick clarif — when you say "log API key usage metadata but not prompt content" — can you state exactly which fields are captured for a request? we need to map to our compliance matrix.

[01:25] Sofia: yes — each request log entry includes timestamp, request id, actor id (user or service), actor role, action type (generate, embed, create_key, etc.), model variant, response size in tokens, latency, source IP, user agent, and a reference to the KV cache hit/miss and cache key if relevant. we also include before/after state for admin changes — e.g., role assignment old/new. note: the transcription sometimes says "KV cash" in older exports, but schema is KV cache.

[02:05] Oliver: do you capture raw customer content anywhere by default? like full prompts or model outputs?

[02:12] Sofia: by default for hosted customers we store request metadata and short traces, not full prompt text — full-text logging is opt-in and flagged as a higher retention category. in dedicated/private deployments customers can choose to retain transcripts or disable them. for cascade, we can set policy to avoid storing full request payloads in the control plane and only stream metadata.

[02:40] Liam: export options — we run a centralized s3+splunk stack. can you forward logs to our s3 bucket or push to splunk?

[02:50] Ethan: yes — we support three main export channels out of the box: 1) streaming to customer-managed S3 (encrypted with customer KMS if you want), 2) syslog/rsyslog or a syslog endpoint for SIEMs like Splunk/Sumo/Datadog, and 3) webhook or Kafka stream for real-time consumers. we also support batch export of historical logs for compliance audits.

[03:18] Rashmi: about encryption — is it provider-managed KMS or can we bring our own key?

[03:24] Sofia: hosted customers default to Redwood-managed KMS. for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS or HSM integrations. when you choose CMK, logs at rest in the export destination (e.g., S3) will be encrypted with your key. note: some older doc pages refer to "custome KMS" — typo, but capability exists.

[03:50] Oliver: retention policy? we need 7 years for some audit trails, other teams want 90 days. what's configurable?

[03:57] Ethan: default for hosted is 90 days for detailed audit logs, 365 days for summarized billing/usage aggregates. For enterprise customers we can extend retention to multi-year or support streaming to customer S3 for indefinite retention and legal hold. Dedicated/Private customers can set retention via config or keep everything in their own storage.

[04:30] Liam: how about immutability / WORM for logs? legal wants tamper-evidence.

[04:36] Sofia: we offer write-once archival to S3 Glacier or use S3 Object Lock (Governance/Compliance mode) when streaming to customer-managed S3. For hosted-original storage we maintain strict access controls and append-only audit store, and we can provide attestations in SOC2 reports.

[05:05] Rashmi: can we get a sample schema? we want to map fields to our SIEM dashboards.

[05:12] Ethan: yes — we'll share the audit log schema and a sample csv/json export. action item: ethan to send schema + SOC2 report and the whitepaper.

[05:30] Oliver: in terms of RBAC/SSO — which admin actions are tied to roles vs service principals? if someone uses an API key, how do you attribute actions?

[05:45] Sofia: actor attribution order: authenticated user (SSO) > service principal > API key owner. for API keys we store key id and the owner user/service mapped at creation time. When keys are rotated we keep rotation history and log who rotated which key. Role-based restrictions are enforced at the control plane; any admin change creates a before/after diff in the log.

[06:20] Liam: any limitations around streaming throughput? we're expecting 20k events/day during pilot bursts.

[06:27] Sofia: that's small — we handle continuous streaming and burst buffering. we have configurable batching to avoid rate-limiting upstream SIEMs. for very high volumes we recommend dedicated log exporters or letting us push to your SQS/Kafka.

[06:46] Rashmi: auditability — do you include IPs and geo, and can you redact fields before export?

[06:53] Sofia: yes we include source IP and geo derived. We support field-level redaction rules during export — e.g., redact user_email or hashed it. However, redaction is a policy layer; if you require absolute zero exposure we recommend exporting to your customer-managed S3 and applying your own transformations.

[07:20] Ethan: to recap: we capture rich admin events, provide streaming/batch export, support CMK for Dedicated/Private, and retention is configurable including legal holds. next steps are sending docs and doing a short pilot.

[07:32] Liam: ok that sounds good. rashmi — anything else?

[07:36] Rashmi: one last question — audit trails for console UI actions vs API calls; are both captured the same way?

[07:44] Sofia: yes, console actions are converted into the same audit events with actor, session id, UI action path, and before/after states. sometimes the auto transcriber marks UI as "you I" in older schema exports, just ignore that.

[08:05] Oliver: timeline for pilot? can we start next week?

[08:09] Ethan: we can; suggested flow: ethan sends schema + security docs by Tues (6/22), sofia sets up an export config and a short-lived token for a one-week pilot (6/23-6/30), cascade provides S3 bucket + IAM role info by 6/24.

[08:30] Rashmi: do you have any SOC2/ISO artefacts we can review?

[08:35] Ethan: yes we'll attach SOC2 Type II report and our security whitepaper. also can provide compliance contact if you need more legal attestations.

[08:52] Liam: what about alerting on suspicious admin activity? do you ship alerts or do we handle in Splunk?

[08:58] Sofia: we can emit structured events with severity heuristics into your SIEM; Redwood Console also has anomaly detection for admin spikes and can raise incidents. many customers prefer SIEM rules for final triage.

[09:18] Rashmi: one operational quirk — if someone deletes a user, do you keep their historical events?

[09:24] Sofia: yes, deletion removes future authentication but historical audit events remain with actor id and a tombstone marker (we do not purge historical records unless an explicit retention policy kicked in).

[09:42] Ethan: any blockers from your side?

[09:45] Liam: none immediate. rashmi will review docs then we'll approve pilot.

[09:50] Rashmi: also please include a sample of the before/after diffs for role changes and SSO config changes.

[09:58] Ethan: will do.

[10:00] (wrap up) Ethan: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with notes and the items discussed.
